hook: Vercel’s CDN billing mode and function configuration matter more than the old five-minute and transfer-overage headline. New Pro teams use Flat Rate CDN by default; eligible functions can run up to 30 minutes in beta. Compare the actual account plan with Cloudflare’s trigger-specific CPU limits, not an assumed universal bill.

sections.title: Identify the CDN billing mode before doing arithmetic
sections.content:
Correction, November 14, 2026: the previous fixed transfer surcharge and migration recommendation are withdrawn. They treated legacy usage-based CDN assumptions as universal and mixed transfer units without verifying the account’s billing mode.

Vercel’s September 2026 Flat Rate CDN announcement says new Pro teams default to that mode; existing teams can switch. Its included tier is 1M CDN requests and 1 TB transfer, not a universal 10M-request allowance.

The announced additional $20/month tier includes 10M requests and 50 TB; $100/month includes 50M and 50 TB. These are CDN capacity tiers, not full hosting invoices.

Usage-based teams have a different regional bill. Read the actual team subscription, capacity, spike-protection and fair-use terms before quoting a total; Cloudflare’s Workers request meter is not interchangeable with Vercel CDN requests.

sections.title: Waiting uses no active CPU, but it is not a free deployment
sections.content:
Fluid compute separates active CPU, provisioned memory and invocation charges. Network waiting need not consume active CPU, but memory, delivery and other services can still cost money.

Workers Standard charges a $5 monthly minimum with 10M requests and 30M CPU-ms included, then $0.30 per million requests and $0.02 per million CPU-ms. Other Cloudflare products have their own meters.

Do not compare a CDN-only price with an application total. Classify static delivery, dynamic invocations, CPU, memory, storage, database access and logs separately; apply only the allowances available to that account.

Workers WebSockets bill the initial Upgrade request, not each routed message as a request; executed code can still consume CPU. Durable Objects are separate: incoming messages use a 20:1 request-billing ratio, and active non-hibernating objects can incur duration charges. “Messages cost nothing” is not a valid total-cost claim.

sections.title: Vercel duration is not a universal five-minute maximum
sections.content:
On Fluid compute, the documented baseline is 300 seconds by default, with Hobby capped at 300 and Pro/Enterprise ordinarily up to 800 seconds. The extended-duration beta allows up to 1,800 seconds for supported Node.js, Bun and Python versions on Pro/Enterprise.

Above 800 seconds, configure each function in code or vercel.json; the project-level default does not enable that duration. Current docs support Secure Compute and Static IPs, but exclude BYOC above 800 seconds during beta.

A duration limit measures elapsed execution, not just active CPU. Non-Fluid projects, other runtimes and upstream/client connection timeouts need separate checks. Inspect the deployed function’s configuration rather than assuming an advertised maximum applies.

sections.title: Cloudflare CPU and wall time depend on the trigger
sections.content:
Workers Paid HTTP CPU defaults to 30 seconds and can be configured up to 5 minutes. Paid Cron has 30 seconds CPU below a one-hour schedule interval, or 15 minutes CPU at intervals of at least one hour.

Queue consumers default to 30 seconds CPU, configurable to 5 minutes; their separate wall-clock limit is 15 minutes. A 15-minute elapsed-time allowance does not authorize 15 minutes of CPU.

These execution limits are separate from Pages deployment limits. Pages documents a 25 MiB asset limit and a 20-minute build timeout; a build or static asset is not a Worker invocation.

Check Free, legacy and account-specific settings separately. A long background job should be assessed for runtime, retry and queue behavior, not selected from a single maximum-duration number.

sections.title: Workers Caching saves CPU, not billed requests
sections.content:
Workers Caching hits remain billed requests at the normal rate even when the Worker does not execute. This also covers static-asset and worker-to-worker requests served through that cache. Ordinary static-asset delivery outside Workers Caching has a separate free request rule.

At 50M requests and 7 ms CPU per execution, uncached Workers Standard is $23.40. With 80% Workers Caching hits, the request overage stays $12; 10M executions use 70M CPU-ms, costing $0.80 above the 30M allowance. Total: $5 + $12 + $0.80 = $17.80, excluding other services.

A Cache API lookup inside running code is different: that code executes and consumes CPU. Do not derive billed requests from execution count. Check cache configuration and measured CPU, and never cache private responses as public.

sections.title: Choose with a complete bill and a deployment test
sections.content:
Do not migrate merely because traffic passes an old request or transfer threshold. Existing Vercel subscriptions and newer Flat Rate CDN teams can have materially different delivery bills.

Compare the same workload and period, using explicit units and the account’s actual rates. Add seats, compute, storage and database costs, plus migration and maintenance effort.

For Pages, test framework compatibility, large assets and build duration. For Vercel, verify function runtime, Fluid compute, configured duration and CDN mode; for Workers, separate HTTP, Cron and Queue limits.

Keep the current platform when its measured total and operational fit are better. The public figures here are reference conditions, not a quote for an inspected customer account.

decision_matrix.why: Flat Rate CDN differs from usage-based regional billing; no universal transfer surcharge is established.
A migration must beat the complete current bill and transition effort, not a single meter.
Active CPU can exclude waiting while memory and other services remain billable.
Pages asset limits apply before traffic pricing; verify the alternative storage and host limits.
Pages build timeout is separate from request execution duration.
Pro/Enterprise baseline reaches 800 seconds; supported-runtime extended beta allows 1,800 seconds.

decision_matrix.situation: Hourly Cron using minutes of CPU
decision_matrix.why: Paid schedules at least one hour apart permit 15 minutes CPU, subject to other limits.

decision_matrix.pick: Do not infer support from wall time
decision_matrix.why: Cloudflare Queue CPU is configurable to 5 minutes; its 15-minute wall limit is separate.

cost_math.label: Workers Standard: 50M requests at 7 ms CPU
cost_math.result: $23.40 modeled base + request + CPU; other services excluded

cost_math.label: Workers Caching: 50M requests, 80% hits, 7 ms per execution
cost_math.result: $17.80; cached requests remain metered, only execution CPU falls; other services excluded

cost_math.label: Vercel Flat Rate CDN capacity reference
cost_math.formula: Published additional CDN tier: $20/month for 10M requests and 50 TB; $100/month for 50M requests and 50 TB
cost_math.result: Capacity tiers only, not total Vercel cost; check billing mode and account terms

cost_math.label: Vercel extended duration configuration
cost_math.result: Supported-runtime Pro/Enterprise beta, per-function opt-in; not a universal default

verdict_summary: The previous automatic recommendation to leave Vercel above a traffic threshold is withdrawn. Compare actual CDN billing mode, complete usage costs and runtime compatibility. Vercel’s extended function duration and Cloudflare’s trigger-specific CPU limits must be checked independently; neither a CDN tier nor an isolated request price is an all-in quote.

faqs.q: Does every Vercel Pro team include 10M CDN requests?
faqs.a: No. The Flat Rate CDN announcement lists 1M requests and 1 TB included with Pro, with additional capacity tiers. New Pro teams use that mode by default; existing teams can differ. Verify the actual billing mode and terms.

faqs.q: Is five minutes the Vercel function maximum?
faqs.a: Not universally. Fluid compute Pro/Enterprise normally supports up to 800 seconds, with an extended beta up to 1,800 seconds for supported runtimes using per-function configuration. Hobby, non-Fluid and BYOC conditions differ.

faqs.q: Can Cloudflare Queue consumers use 15 minutes of CPU?
faqs.a: Current Queues documentation specifies 30 seconds CPU by default, configurable to 5 minutes. Its wall-clock limit is 15 minutes. Paid Cron scheduled at least hourly has a separate 15-minute CPU allowance.

faqs.q: Are these figures complete hosting invoices?
faqs.a: No. CDN capacity, request overage and CPU calculations cover different meters. Include plan charges, available quotas, memory, storage, database use and other applicable services before comparing totals.
